clue.text: Sailing from land with a very big black cast-away aboard

indicators.note: aboard says the following pieces go inside the word for land, as passengers ride inside a ship

parts.note: a land is a nation

indicators.note: cast away says the named letter is thrown out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written before the letter is removed
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A castaway aboard a ship sailing away from land, a big black figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black' is not a colour of the castaway but the pencil letter that 'cast-away' throws out; 'aboard' signals the insertion, as passengers board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigation is the art of steering a ship, so it can stand for sailing as an activity.

clue.text: Recently developed shopping centre in a racing town

parts.note: something recently developed is new
a market is a place for buying goods

explanation.surface: A new mall has opened in a horse-racing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket in Suffolk is the centre of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is an English town famous as the headquarters of flat racing.

clue.text: Rented holiday home in very bad area

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A holiday let located in a rough neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a house, often hired by tourists for a holiday abroad.

clue.text: Nag a nude girl, a free spirit

indicators.note: free says the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pestering a naked girl, a free spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free spirit' looks like one phrase, but 'free' is the anagram signal and 'spirit' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protective spirit thought to watch over a person.

clue.text: Italian artist to draw game

parts.note: to tie a match is to draw it
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: An Italian painter sketches a sporting game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests an artist sketching, but it means to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Becomes more communicative and frank with drink

parts.note: frank means open, honest
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone becomes chatty and candid after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening up is the idiom for starting to talk freely about oneself.

clue.text: Endless industrial action in a Scandinavian port

indicators.note: endless says the phrase loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately work slowly

explanation.surface: A labour dispute disrupting a harbour in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims G and W from GOSLOW. A go-slow is a British name for a protest in which staff work at a deliberately reduced pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the Norwegian capital and a seaport on its fjord.

clue.text: Put up in part of Ceylon —- a paradise

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
part of says only the opening portion of the name is used

parts.note: Ceylon is the former name of Sri Lanka
to put up a picture is to hang it

explanation.surface: Staying in part of Ceylon felt like heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Ceylon is the old name of the island nation; 'part of' takes only its opening letters, and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the fictional Himalayan utopia from Hilton's novel, hence any earthly paradise.

clue.text: Clear above top of tower

parts.note: over means above

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter, the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: A clear view from above the top of a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, so clear.

clue.text: Fence associated with excellent crime writer

parts.note: a fence is a kind of wall, a barrier round a field
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A receiver of stolen goods linked with a top-rate detective novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' suggests a receiver of stolen goods, fitting the crime surface, but here it is simply a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific English thriller writer, creator of King Kong's story.

clue.text: Revolving handle getting a note to emerge

indicators.note: revolving says the word for handle is turned round

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A turning door handle letting out a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolving' turns NAME into EMAN. 'Handle' looks like a knob but is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so it means to emerge.

clue.text: Writer's two articles getting to the Parisian, being connected with his country

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article
taken as written
le is French for the
the writer's country is France

explanation.surface: A writer's two pieces reach a Parisian reader, tied to his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Writer's' means 'has'. 'his country' refers back to the French writer, a nation fair to name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatole France was a French novelist who won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: A flipping tie may help one to get a prize

indicators.note: flipping says the word for tie is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a tie in a match is a draw

explanation.surface: A tied match might help someone win a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns DRAW into WARD; 'may help one to get' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something granted for merit, a synonym of prize.

clue.text: Sally foolishly hangs out about 50

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the numeral
foolishly says the letters are mixed up without sense

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A girl named Sally hangs around rather pointlessly, at about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a sudden attack. 'foolishly' rearranges HANGSOUT, and 'about' puts it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden charge out against an enemy, much like an onslaught or fierce assault.

clue.text: Held on to a Colonel Blimp drawing that's stayed out of the public eye?

definitions.text: stayed out of the public eye

parts.note: to retain something is to keep it, past tense kept
Colonel Blimp was created by the cartoonist David Low, so a drawing of him is a Low profile

explanation.surface: Someone clung to a cartoon of a pompous colonel and stayed hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp, a pompous reactionary officer, was a 1930s British newspaper cartoon by David Low, so his side view is a 'Low profile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a low profile is the idiom for avoiding attention and publicity.

clue.text: Extinct reptile shown in a poster flying over ancient city

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in a down clue
flying suggests the letters scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Sumer

explanation.surface: A dinosaur depicted on a poster soaring above an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges A POSTER into PTEROSA, placed 'over' UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pterosaur is an extinct flying reptile of the Mesozoic era, such as the pterodactyl.

clue.text: Last always, reportedly, to make an industrious effort

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: last is end and always is ever, giving end ever

explanation.surface: Persisting to the very end is what hard work takes.
explanation.walkthrough: END plus EVER, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard or strive at something.

clue.text: The best that is obtainable for our heavyweights?

definitions.text: The best that is obtainable for our heavyweights?

parts.words: The best that is obtainable for our heavyweights?
parts.note: the idiom for the richest produce available is read literally as the portly folk who own the country

explanation.surface: A wry question about who gets the choicest things.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical idiom means the best of everything; the question mark invites reading 'fat' as heavyweights.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Genesis means the finest resources or luxuries available.

clue.text: Working with sailor, one round lake

parts.note: on means working, as in switched on
a tar is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A sailor at work going round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Traitor's initial motive for his crime?

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: Asking what first drove a traitor to his deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is the specific offence a traitor commits.

clue.text: Material girl

definitions.meaning: a thin silk or crepe dress fabric
a girl's first name, a feminine form of George

explanation.definitionFit: Georgette is both a sheer crêpe fabric and a woman's name.

clue.text: Rouse oneself and dress

definitions.meaning: an outfit, often an odd one

explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to rise; a get-up is a costume or outfit.

clue.text: Indian dish (some pakora) it advertised

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Indian restaurant advertising a pakora side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yogurt side dish from Indian cuisine, often with cucumber.

clue.text: Model of one member of Cinque port confederation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Deal in Kent was a limb of the Cinque Ports, a medieval alliance of south-coast towns

explanation.surface: A model town from the old Kentish coastal league.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports were a medieval group of English Channel ports in Kent and Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or standard to copy, a model.

clue.text: Creeping plant in house on wheels

definitions.meaning: a plant that trails along the ground or a wall
a towed mobile home, in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a trailing plant and also a caravan or mobile home in American English.

clue.text: Unusual sermon about a Ligurian resort

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the article
unusual says the letters of the word are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange sermon preached about a seaside town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges SERMON into SNREMO, and 'about' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanremo is a resort town on the Italian Riviera in the region of Liguria.

clue.text: Parking with skill — and that's not all

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Parking skilfully is only half the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is only a portion of something, not the whole of it.

clue.text: Therapist one elected locally to listen to

indicators.note: to listen to says the word sounds like another when heard

parts.note: a councillor is an elected member of a local council

explanation.surface: A therapist is someone you go to so they listen to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words for a local councillor and a counselling therapist are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A counsellor gives professional guidance on personal problems, a kind of therapist.
